## A. Vocabulary hunt

Go to the paragraph in the reading (¶3 = paragraph 3). Find the word that matches the clue and write it in the Word box. A bold word part (**un-**, **-ly**) means the word has that prefix or suffix.

::: vocab-hunt
- ¶1 | *n.* a group of lands ruled by one leader | empire
- ¶1 | *n.* people who fight in an army | soldiers
- ¶1 | *n.* a long trip | journey
- ¶2 | *n.* one level of material on top of another | layer
- ¶2 | *n.* small stones | gravel
- ¶2 | *adj.* bent like part of a circle | curved
- ¶2 | *v.* to let water flow away | drain
- ¶2 | *adj.* strong; hard to break | sturdy
- ¶3 | *n.* a stone that shows how far you have come | milestone
- ¶3 | *n.* people who buy and sell things | merchants
- ¶4 | **-er** *n.* people who make things | builders
- ¶4 | *n.* a channel or bridge that carries water | aqueduct
- ¶4 | *n.* the force that pulls things down | gravity
- ¶4 | *n.* a surface that goes slowly up or down | slope
- ¶5 | *n.* low land between hills | valley
- ¶5 | *n.* curved shapes that hold up a bridge | arches
- ¶5 | **un-** *adj.* still in one piece | unbroken
- ¶6 | **-ly** *adv.* with great care | carefully
- ¶6 | **-ous** *adj.* known by many people | famous
- ¶6 | *v.* to fix | repair
:::

::: {.panel title="Word parts"}
**un-** = not · **-er** = a person who · **-ly** = in this way · **-ous** = full of
:::

::: {.recall lines="2"}
- The reading is called "Roads that held an empire." Give it a new title, then explain your title. | All Roads Lead to Rome: the roads joined every city to Rome.
:::

{{< pagebreak >}}

## B. Reading recall

Answer each question in a complete sentence.

::: recall
- Why did Rome need roads? | To move soldiers, letters and food quickly around the empire.
- What were the layers of a Roman road? | Large stones, then gravel and sand, then flat paving stones.
- Why was the top of the road curved? | So rain ran off to the sides and the road stayed dry.
- How did water move along an aqueduct without pumps? | Gravity: the channel sloped gently downhill all the way.
:::

## C. Building a road

Number the steps from 1 to 6 in the order the builders did them.

::: {.sequence order="4,1,6,2,5,3"}
- Lay flat paving stones on top.
- Dig a deep trench.
- Put up a milestone every Roman mile.
- Fill the bottom with large stones.
- Make the top curved so rain runs off.
- Add a layer of gravel and sand.
:::
